acid-base-disorders.name: Acid-base disorders
acid-base-disorders.scope: Metabolic acidosis (anion gap, non-anion gap), metabolic alkalosis (saline-responsive vs saline-resistant), respiratory acidosis, respiratory alkalosis, Winter formula, mixed disorders
acid-base-disorders.core: Identify the primary pH disturbance, test expected compensation, then investigate the anion gap or urine chloride to locate the cause.

rows.label: Definition
items: Acidemia: pH <7.35; alkalemia: >7.45; normal pH can hide opposing primary disorders
Metabolic: primary HCO3 change; respiratory: primary PaCO2 change

rows.label: Formula
items: ★ **AG = Na − (Cl + HCO3)**; usual normal ≈8–12, laboratory dependent
Hypoalbuminemia correction: add 2.5 to AG per 1 g/dL albumin below 4
★ **Winter: expected PaCO2 = 1.5 × HCO3 + 8 ±2**

rows.label: Interpret
items: HCO3 12 → expected PaCO2 26 ±2; measured 40 → additional respiratory acidosis
Metabolic alkalosis: expected PaCO2 ≈40 + 0.7 × (HCO3 − 24), ±5
Respiratory HCO3 change per 10 PaCO2: acidosis +1 acute/+4 chronic; alkalosis −2 acute/−4 chronic

rows.label: Use when
items: ★ Alkalosis: **urine Cl <20 mmol/L** → saline-responsive; ≥20 → diuretics/mineralocorticoids
ΔAG exceeds HCO3 fall → additional alkalosis; smaller ΔAG → additional non-gap acidosis

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Compensation never overshoots; values outside expected range imply **mixed disorder**
Salicylates often cause respiratory alkalosis plus high-gap acidosis; near-normal pH is deceptive
Diarrhea/RTA: non-gap acidosis; renal failure: either gap pattern

acid-base-disorders.evidence: Established physiologic formulas; no guideline involved.

acne-vulgaris.name: Acne vulgaris
acne-vulgaris.scope: Comedonal, inflammatory, and nodulocystic acne, topical retinoids, benzoyl peroxide, oral antibiotics, isotretinoin, photosensitivity counseling
acne-vulgaris.core: Open or closed comedones with variable inflammatory papules, pustules, or nodules reflect pilosebaceous inflammation; severity and scarring determine treatment intensity.

rows.label: Risk factors

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Follicular hyperkeratinization + sebum + Cutibacterium acnes-driven inflammation
Topical retinoids normalize follicular shedding; benzoyl peroxide is bactericidal without antibiotic resistance

rows.label: Dx

Hyperandrogenic findings → pregnancy test and targeted testosterone/DHEAS evaluation
Before isotretinoin → pregnancy assessment when applicable, baseline lipids and liver enzymes; monitor during treatment

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Combine topical mechanisms** and match intensity below; improvement requires weeks, maintenance prevents relapse
★ **Antibiotics require the topical backbone below**; never antibiotic monotherapy; limit systemic course
Adult hormonally driven acne → combined contraceptive or spironolactone when suitable; avoid spironolactone in pregnancy
★ Isotretinoin → **strict pregnancy prevention/testing**; avoid pregnancy during treatment and 1 month afterward
Pregnancy → azelaic acid/benzoyl peroxide options; avoid retinoids and tetracyclines

Doxycycline → esophagitis/photosensitivity; isotretinoin → cheilitis, hypertriglyceridemia, hepatotoxicity
Avoid simultaneous isotretinoin + tetracycline because intracranial hypertension risk

rows.label: Mimics
items: Rosacea: flushing/telangiectasia without comedones

Perioral dermatitis: periorificial papules, vermilion sparing, steroid exposure

acute-coronary-syndromes.name: Acute coronary syndromes
acute-coronary-syndromes.scope: Unstable angina, NSTEMI, STEMI, cardiac biomarkers, risk stratification (HEART/TIMI), antiplatelet and anticoagulation, reperfusion
acute-coronary-syndromes.core: Acute myocardial ischemia from coronary plaque disruption: distinguish occlusive infarction needing immediate reperfusion from non-ST-elevation syndromes needing risk-guided invasive management.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Smoking, diabetes, hypertension, dyslipidemia, CKD, age, premature family CAD
Cocaine/stimulants, anemia, tachyarrhythmia may provoke ischemia; distinguish supply-demand injury from plaque rupture

rows.label: Clues
items: Pressure with arm/jaw radiation, diaphoresis, nausea; older adults/diabetes may have dyspnea alone

★ New murmur, pulmonary edema, shock after MI → **mechanical complication**, urgent echo

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Platelet activation and thrombin-mediated clot reduce coronary perfusion; necrosis releases troponin
Type 2 MI: oxygen mismatch without acute atherothrombosis; treat precipitating cause

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **ECG within 10 minutes**, repeat if nondiagnostic; serial high-sensitivity troponin using validated pathway
Posterior suspicion → V7–V9; inferior MI → right-sided leads; new LBBB alone insufficient for STEMI
★ **Do not wait for troponin before STEMI reperfusion**; bedside echo if diagnosis/complications uncertain
HEART ≤3 + negative serial troponins → low risk; TIMI/GRACE stratifies NSTE-ACS

Pericarditis: positional pleuritic pain, diffuse changes
PE: hypoxemia, thrombotic risk, RV strain

rows: Urgent catheterization if unstable; otherwise risk-guided angiography
Regional ST elevation or occlusion equivalent
Prior intracranial hemorrhage, active bleeding, suspected dissection

acute-kidney-injury.name: Acute kidney injury
acute-kidney-injury.core: Abrupt loss of renal filtration: separate impaired perfusion, parenchymal injury, and urinary obstruction before treating the cause.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Volume depletion, sepsis, heart failure, cirrhosis; baseline CKD increases vulnerability
NSAIDs constrict afferent arterioles; ACE inhibitors/ARBs reduce efferent tone during hypoperfusion
Aminoglycosides, pigment injury, prolonged ischemia → tubular damage; antibiotics/PPIs → interstitial inflammation

rows.label: Clues
items: Oliguria, edema, uremic nausea; urine output may remain normal
AIN: fever, rash, eosinophilia sometimes present; classic triad often absent
★ Pulmonary edema, severe hyperkalemia, encephalopathy, pericarditis → **urgent renal support**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Reduced glomerular pressure, tubular epithelial injury, or backpressure → declining GFR

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ AKI: creatinine ↑≥0.3 mg/dL within 48 h, ≥1.5-fold within 7 days, or oliguria
Oliguria criterion: urine <0.5 mL/kg/h for ≥6 h; trend creatinine, electrolytes, fluid balance
★ **Urinalysis + microscopy**, medication review; bladder scan → renal ultrasound if obstruction possible
FeNa unreliable with diuretics, CKD, early obstruction; urine eosinophils neither sensitive nor specific
Unexplained persistent injury or suspected glomerulonephritis → nephrology, possible kidney biopsy

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Severe hyperkalemia → **IV calcium**, insulin/dextrose; refractory electrolyte disturbance → dialysis
Hypovolemia → isotonic crystalloid; congestion → loop diuretic; avoid reflex fluids in overloaded patients
Stop culprit nephrotoxins; renal-dose drugs; AIN persisting after withdrawal → consider glucocorticoids
★ Obstruction → **catheter or ureteral decompression**; monitor postobstructive diuresis
Dialysis: refractory acidosis, hyperkalemia, intoxication, overload, symptomatic uremia; no isolated creatinine threshold

rows.label: Complications
items: Arrhythmias, acidosis, volume overload; subsequent CKD
Recovery diuresis → dehydration and electrolyte losses

rows.label: Prevention
items: Maintain perfusion during illness; review nephrotoxic combinations and monitor renal function

rows.label: Mimics
items: CKD: longstanding abnormalities, small echogenic kidneys, chronic anemia
Trimethoprim effect: creatinine rise without true GFR decline

acute-kidney-injury.evidence: Not checked online; established KDIGO diagnostic criteria and renal teaching.

anaphylaxis.name: Anaphylaxis
anaphylaxis.scope: Anaphylaxis, angioedema, biphasic reactions, epinephrine autoinjector, emergency airway management
anaphylaxis.core: Rapid multisystem reaction after exposure—or isolated hypotension or airway compromise after a known allergen—requires epinephrine immediately.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Foods, insect venom, antibiotics, latex; exercise can amplify food-triggered reactions
Asthma, prior severe reaction, mast-cell disorders; beta-blockers can complicate treatment

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Urticaria/angioedema + wheeze, stridor, hypotension, or severe GI symptoms**
Skin findings may be absent; hoarseness and tongue swelling predict airway danger
Biphasic recurrence after apparent resolution, especially after severe or undertreated episodes

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Mast-cell/basophil mediators → vasodilation, capillary leak, bronchoconstriction; often IgE-mediated

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical diagnosis**; never wait for tryptase or laboratory confirmation
Acute and baseline serum tryptase can support uncertain cases; normal results do not exclude anaphylaxis

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **IM epinephrine 0.01 mg/kg**, adult 0.3–0.5 mg, lateral thigh; repeat every 5–15 minutes
Supine with legs elevated unless respiratory distress; oxygen, IV saline, early intubation for progressive obstruction
Refractory shock → monitored IV epinephrine infusion; beta-blocker-associated refractory reaction → glucagon
Albuterol for residual bronchospasm; antihistamines relieve itching only; steroids do not reliably prevent biphasic reactions
★ Monitor until resolved; **longer observation/admission** after hypotension, repeated epinephrine, or severe asthma

rows.label: Complications
items: Asphyxia, distributive shock, arrhythmia, hypoxic brain injury
IV epinephrine bolus errors → ischemia and dangerous dysrhythmia

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Prescribe **epinephrine autoinjector**, demonstrate technique, provide written action plan and allergy referral
Extra device for repeat-dose risk; avoidance, medical alert ID; venom immunotherapy after qualifying sting allergy

rows.label: Mimics
items: Vasovagal episode: bradycardia, pallor, rapid improvement supine
Bradykinin angioedema: no itching/hives; ACE inhibitor or hereditary disease → airway, icatibant/C1 inhibitor

aortic-dissection.name: Aortic dissection
aortic-dissection.core: Sudden maximal chest or back pain with vascular or neurologic deficits suggests aortic dissection, even without widened mediastinum.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Long-standing hypertension, bicuspid aortic valve, coarctation
Marfan/vascular Ehlers-Danlos, pregnancy, cocaine, aortic instrumentation or aneurysm

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Abrupt severe pain**, pulse/BP asymmetry, syncope, focal neurologic deficit
New aortic regurgitation murmur; limb ischemia or abdominal pain from branch-vessel malperfusion
Hypotension suggests rupture, tamponade, severe regurgitation, or coronary involvement

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Intimal tear → blood separates medial layers, creating false lumen
Propagation compromises branch arteries or ruptures into pericardium/pleura

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Stable → **CTA chest/abdomen/pelvis**; unstable or unable to leave resuscitation → bedside TEE
Chest radiograph may show widened mediastinum but normal film does not exclude dissection
ECG/troponin may mimic MI; high suspicion requires aortic imaging before antithrombotics
Examine bilateral arm pressures, femoral pulses, neurologic status, renal function

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **IV esmolol or labetalol** + opioid analgesia; target HR 60–80 and SBP <120 if perfusion maintained
Persistent hypertension after rate control → nicardipine; avoid vasodilator before beta blockade
★ **Avoid anticoagulation and thrombolysis** when dissection suspected
Tamponade from dissection → immediate surgical team; routine pericardiocentesis can worsen hemorrhage

rows.label: Complications
items: Aortic rupture, hemothorax, tamponade, MI, stroke, paraplegia, mesenteric/renal ischemia
Late aneurysmal dilation or recurrent dissection despite initial successful treatment

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Lifelong **BP control and surveillance CTA/MRA**; beta-blocker-based regimen
Avoid heavy isometric lifting; screen first-degree relatives for familial aortopathy

rows.label: Mimics
items: Acute coronary syndrome: pressure-like pain, no pulse deficit; coexistence possible
PE: pleuritic pain, hypoxemia, right-heart strain
Esophageal rupture: vomiting followed by pain and subcutaneous emphysema

aortic-dissection.evidence: Not checked online; established aortic emergency principles.

asthma.name: Asthma
asthma.scope: Diagnosis, stepwise therapy, acute exacerbation, exercise-induced bronchoconstriction
asthma.core: Variable episodes of wheeze, cough, dyspnea, and chest tightness from reversible expiratory airflow limitation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Atopy, family history, allergens, viral infections, smoke, occupational sensitizers
Exercise/cold air, aspirin-sensitive disease, nonselective beta-blockers; assess workplace symptom pattern

rows.label: Clues
items: Nocturnal/early-morning symptoms; normal examination between attacks
★ **Silent chest, exhaustion, altered mentation, rising PaCO2** → impending respiratory failure
Acute attack: low peak flow, accessory-muscle use, difficulty speaking

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Airway inflammation, smooth-muscle constriction, mucus → variable obstruction and hyperresponsiveness
Persistent uncontrolled inflammation → remodeling with incompletely reversible airflow limitation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Spirometry**: obstruction with bronchodilator FEV1 increase >12% and >200 mL in adults
Normal spirometry with suspicion → repeat during symptoms or methacholine challenge
Exercise challenge: postexercise FEV1 fall >10%; assess baseline control before isolated exercise diagnosis

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Exacerbation → **repeated inhaled albuterol + ipratropium**, oxygen, early systemic glucocorticoids
Severe poor response → IV magnesium; deterioration → intubation; avoid sedatives and routine antibiotics
Exercise symptoms → preexercise albuterol or prescribed ICS-formoterol; persistent symptoms → improve controller
Check technique/adherence before stepping up; uncontrolled despite high-dose ICS-LABA → phenotype-directed biologic referral

rows.label: Complications
items: Status asthmaticus, pneumothorax, respiratory arrest
ICS → thrush/dysphonia; systemic steroids → osteoporosis, hyperglycemia, adrenal suppression

rows.label: Prevention
items: Written action plan, trigger reduction, smoking cessation, spacer; rinse mouth after ICS
★ **No SABA-only treatment or LABA monotherapy**; current GINA differs from older intermittent-asthma teaching

rows.label: Mimics
items: Inducible laryngeal obstruction: inspiratory stridor, inspiratory flow-loop flattening
COPD: persistent obstruction, smoking history
HF: edema, elevated JVP, cardiac findings

benign-prostatic-hyperplasia.name: Benign prostatic hyperplasia
benign-prostatic-hyperplasia.scope: Lower urinary tract symptoms, medical therapy, urinary retention and obstructive uropathy
benign-prostatic-hyperplasia.core: Aging man with hesitancy, weak stream, incomplete emptying, and nocturia from benign periurethral prostatic enlargement.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Increasing age, androgen exposure, family history, obesity/metabolic syndrome
Anticholinergics, opioids, and sympathomimetic decongestants can precipitate retention

rows.label: Clues
items: Storage symptoms: urgency, frequency; voiding symptoms: straining, intermittency, terminal dribbling
Smooth, symmetric enlarged prostate; size correlates imperfectly with symptom severity
★ **Painful inability to void** with palpable bladder → acute urinary retention
Renal dysfunction or bilateral hydronephrosis suggests high-pressure obstruction

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Dihydrotestosterone-driven transition-zone hyperplasia + alpha-adrenergic smooth-muscle tone obstruct bladder outlet

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Urinalysis**, symptom score, examination; review medications and neurologic disease
Postvoid residual if incomplete emptying suspected; creatinine/renal ultrasound for obstruction or renal impairment
PSA after shared decision-making if result changes management; elevation not specific for cancer

rows.label: Tx
items: Mild, nonbothersome → observation; reduce evening fluids, caffeine, alcohol; timed voiding
★ Acute retention → **urethral catheter**, then alpha-blocker and voiding trial; suprapubic drainage if catheterization fails
★ Refractory symptoms, retention, recurrent UTIs, stones, renal impairment → **TURP or other outlet procedure**
Monitor urine output/electrolytes after relief of prolonged obstruction

rows.label: Complications
items: Overflow incontinence, recurrent infection, bladder stones, postrenal AKI
Postobstructive diuresis; surgery → bleeding, retrograde ejaculation, urethral stricture

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid precipitating drugs; reassess progressive symptoms and residual volume
BPH does not transform into prostate cancer; continue independent cancer-risk discussion

rows.label: Mimics
items: Prostate cancer: hard asymmetric nodule
Prostatitis: tender prostate, fever; neurogenic bladder: neurologic disease, altered bladder sensation

table.title: Medication selection
rows: Large gland; reduce progression over months

dementia.name: Dementia
dementia.scope: Alzheimer, vascular, Lewy body, frontotemporal, reversible causes, normal cognitive aging vs MCI, Parkinson disease dementia
dementia.core: Acquired cognitive decline interfering with independent daily function; distinguish dementia from normal aging and mild cognitive impairment by functional consequences.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Advanced age, family history; vascular risk factors, prior stroke, Parkinson disease
Anticholinergics, sedatives, alcohol, hearing loss, sleep apnea may worsen cognition

rows.label: Clues
items: Collateral history: missed bills/medications, getting lost, unsafe cooking or driving
Personality, language, executive, visuospatial, memory, motor symptoms help establish phenotype
Abrupt change, fluctuating attention, fever, focal deficits → evaluate acute superimposed illness

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Alzheimer: amyloid plaques/tau tangles; Lewy/Parkinson: alpha-synuclein; vascular disease: ischemic neuronal injury
Frontotemporal degeneration affects frontal/anterior temporal networks, often before typical late-life onset

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Patient/informant history, cognition, function**; MoCA/MMSE support diagnosis, cannot establish it alone
★ **CBC, CMP, TSH, B12**, depression/medication review; HIV/syphilis testing if risk
Brain MRI or noncontrast CT → infarcts, mass, subdural, hydrocephalus; avoid routine PET as first test
Normal aging: slower retrieval with preserved independence; MCI: objective deficit without loss of independent function

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Alzheimer/Lewy/Parkinson dementia → **donepezil or rivastigmine**; moderate/severe Alzheimer → add memantine
Vascular disease → BP/lipid/diabetes control, stroke prevention; frontotemporal behavioral symptoms → consider SSRI
★ Agitation → seek pain/infection, routines/redirection first; **avoid typical antipsychotics in Lewy disease**
Early biomarker-confirmed Alzheimer: specialist-selected antiamyloid drugs; baseline/serial MRI for ARIA

rows.label: Complications
items: Falls, aspiration, malnutrition, wandering, caregiver burnout; antipsychotics → increased mortality
Cholinesterase inhibitors → bradycardia, syncope, GI effects; antiamyloid antibodies → edema/microhemorrhage

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Driving/home safety, advance planning**, caregiver support; assess decision-specific capacity
Exercise, hearing correction, social engagement, vascular risk reduction

rows.label: Mimics
items: Delirium: hours–days, impaired attention, fluctuating awareness
Depression: prominent distress, variable effort, potentially reversible cognitive deficits
Normal-pressure hydrocephalus: gait-first decline, incontinence, ventriculomegaly; tap test may predict shunt response

table.title: Phenotype clues
rows: Insidious episodic-memory decline, later multidomain deficits
Stroke-related or stepwise decline, focal findings
Early hallucinations, fluctuation, REM behavior, parkinsonism
Early disinhibition/apathy or progressive aphasia; memory spared
Established motor disease >1 year before dementia

dementia.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [Alzheimer's Association diagnostic guidance 2024](https://www.alz.org/news/2024/clinical-practice-guideline-evaluation-alzheimers), [NICE dementia](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng97/chapter/Recommendations/); established subtype teaching.

dyslipidemia.name: Dyslipidemia
dyslipidemia.scope: Lipid screening guidelines, ASCVD risk calculation, statin therapy indications, monitoring response to diet and pharmacotherapy
dyslipidemia.core: Excess atherogenic lipoproteins drive ASCVD; treatment intensity follows established disease, severe LDL elevation, diabetes, and estimated absolute cardiovascular risk.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Familial disorders, saturated-fat intake, obesity, diabetes, hypothyroidism, nephrotic syndrome, cholestasis
Premature ASCVD family history, CKD, smoking, inflammatory disease increase treatment benefit

rows.label: Clues
items: Usually asymptomatic; tendon xanthomas/early corneal arcus suggest familial hypercholesterolemia
Severe triglyceride elevation: eruptive xanthomas, pancreatitis; low HDL alone is not a drug target

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Retained apoB-containing particles → arterial inflammation and plaque formation
Statins inhibit HMG-CoA reductase → hepatic LDL-receptor upregulation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Lipid panel from age 19, at least every 5 years**; earlier/more often with risk
Nonfasting panel acceptable; markedly high triglycerides → fasting repeat/secondary-cause evaluation; Lp(a) once/lifetime
★ **PREVENT-ASCVD**, ages 30–79, LDL 70–189 without ASCVD: replaces pooled-cohort equations in 2026 guidance
Uncertain statin decision → coronary calcium; zero insufficient for deferral with diabetes, smoking, strong premature history

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Clinical ASCVD or **LDL ≥190 mg/dL → high-intensity statin**, no risk calculation required
★ Diabetes age 40–75 → **at least moderate-intensity statin**; multiple risk factors favor high intensity
Above LDL target despite maximal statin → ezetimibe; consider PCSK9 inhibitor or bempedoic acid
Severe triglycerides ≥500 → address causes, diet, consider fenofibrate/prescription omega-3 to reduce pancreatitis risk

rows.label: Complications
items: MI, stroke, peripheral arterial disease; statins → myalgias, rare rhabdomyolysis, small diabetes-risk increase
Baseline ALT; CK only with symptoms/risk; most lipid-lowering drugs deferred during conception/pregnancy/lactation

rows.label: Prevention
items: Mediterranean-style diet, replace saturated fats, exercise, weight reduction, smoking cessation
★ Recheck lipids **4–12 weeks after starting/changing drugs**, then every 6–12 months; assess adherence
High intensity lowers LDL ≥50%: atorvastatin 40–80 mg or rosuvastatin 20–40 mg

rows.label: Mimics
items: Hypothyroidism: elevated TSH; correct before labeling primary dyslipidemia
Nephrotic syndrome: heavy proteinuria, hypoalbuminemia; treat renal cause

table.title: Risk-based primary prevention and secondary target

gastrointestinal-bleeding.name: Gastrointestinal bleeding
gastrointestinal-bleeding.scope: Upper GI bleeding (PUD, varices, Mallory-Weiss), lower GI bleeding (diverticular, angiodysplasia, hemorrhoids), fluid and transfusion thresholds, endoscopy
gastrointestinal-bleeding.core: Hematemesis, melena, or hematochezia → assess hemodynamics before localizing; brisk upper bleeding can present as bright red rectal blood.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: NSAIDs/H pylori → ulcers; cirrhosis → varices; forceful retching → mucosal tear
Anticoagulants/antiplatelets increase severity; older age favors diverticula or angiodysplasia

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ **Syncope, orthostasis, shock** signal major loss; initial hemoglobin may remain normal
Epigastric pain supports ulcer; painless bleeding favors vascular sources
Recurrent occult loss → iron deficiency; elevated BUN/creatinine ratio supports upper source

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Mucosal injury, portal-pressure collaterals, or fragile vessels rupture into GI lumen
Volume depletion → reduced perfusion; ongoing bleeding may require massive transfusion

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Two large-bore IVs, CBC, type/cross, coagulation tests**, serial hemoglobin; resuscitate before procedures
Upper source → EGD within 24 hours after stabilization; suspected varices → within 12 hours
★ Ongoing hemodynamically significant hematochezia → **CT angiography → embolization** if active extravasation
Stable lower bleeding → bowel preparation and nonemergent colonoscopy; routine <24-hour colonoscopy adds no benefit

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Crystalloid initially; stable nonischemic adults → **RBC transfusion at hemoglobin <7 g/dL**
Active exsanguination → blood immediately regardless of hemoglobin; cardiac ischemia → individualize higher threshold
Severe life-threatening anticoagulant bleeding → drug-specific reversal; persistent bleeding after endoscopy → IR/surgery
Suspected ulcer → IV PPI; endoscopic hemostasis for active bleeding/visible vessel, then high-dose PPI

rows.label: Complications
items: Rebleeding, aspiration, myocardial ischemia, AKI; variceal bleeding → infection
Massive transfusion → hypocalcemia, hypothermia, coagulopathy; embolization → bowel ischemia

rows.label: Prevention
items: Eradicate H pylori and confirm cure; avoid NSAIDs; PPI for high-risk users
After variceal control: nonselective beta-blocker plus repeat banding; recurrent bleeding → TIPS

rows.label: Mimics
items: Iron/bismuth: dark stool without blood loss
Hemoptysis: coughing frothy blood rather than vomiting
Swallowed epistaxis: nasal source on examination

gastrointestinal-bleeding.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [ACG lower GI bleeding 2023](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36735555/), [ACS transfusion guidance 2025](https://www.jacc.org/doi/10.1016/j.jacc.2024.11.009).

gonococcal-infection.name: Gonococcal infection
gonococcal-infection.scope: Urethritis/cervicitis, disseminated gonococcal infection, gonococcal arthritis, neonatal conjunctivitis
gonococcal-infection.core: Neisseria gonorrhoeae causes mucosal infection and can disseminate into a dermatitis-tenosynovitis-arthritis syndrome or purulent septic arthritis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: New/multiple partners, inconsistent barriers, prior STI, younger age
Complement deficiency increases dissemination risk; neonatal exposure during vaginal delivery

rows.label: Clues
items: Dysuria, mucopurulent discharge, friable cervix; rectal/pharyngeal disease often asymptomatic
★ **Migratory arthralgia, tenosynovitis, sparse pustules** → disseminated infection
Neonate: copious purulent conjunctivitis 2–5 days after birth; corneal injury can progress rapidly

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Gram-negative intracellular diplococci adhere to mucosa; antigenic variation permits recurrent infection
Ascending genital spread or bacteremia extends disease beyond initial exposure site

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **NAAT at exposed sites**: urine/vaginal, rectal, pharyngeal; test chlamydia, HIV, syphilis
Symptomatic male urethral Gram stain may show intracellular diplococci; less reliable at other sites
Dissemination: blood/synovial cultures and mucosal NAAT; negative joint culture does not exclude diagnosis
Suspected treatment failure → culture and antimicrobial susceptibility, assess reinfection

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Uncomplicated: **ceftriaxone 500 mg IM once**; ≥150 kg → 1 g once
Chlamydia not excluded → doxycycline for 7 days; pregnancy → azithromycin instead
★ Disseminated disease → **IV/IM ceftriaxone**, hospitalization initially; drain purulent joint
Neonatal infection → systemic ceftriaxone, or cefotaxime if bilirubin/calcium concerns; topical treatment alone insufficient

rows.label: Complications
items: PID, infertility, ectopic pregnancy, epididymitis, corneal perforation
Rare endocarditis/meningitis; untreated septic arthritis damages cartilage

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Treat partners from preceding **60 days**; abstain 7 days after treatment and until partners treated
Retest at 3 months; pharyngeal test-of-cure at 7–14 days; routine urogenital test-of-cure unnecessary
Condoms, risk-based screening; neonatal erythromycin eye ointment prevents gonococcal ophthalmia

rows.label: Mimics
items: Chlamydia: similar urethritis/cervicitis, NAAT distinguishes
Reactive arthritis: sterile arthritis after infection, conjunctivitis/enthesitis
Staphylococcal arthritis: usually isolated hot joint without migratory skin-tendon syndrome

heart-failure.name: Heart failure
heart-failure.scope: HFrEF, HFpEF, acute decompensated heart failure, cardiogenic flash pulmonary edema, guideline-directed medical therapy, neurohormonal activation (RAAS, ADH-mediated hyponatremia)
heart-failure.core: Inadequate cardiac output or elevated filling pressures → pulmonary or systemic congestion, even with a normal ejection fraction.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: CAD, hypertension, valvular disease, cardiomyopathy, alcohol, cardiotoxic chemotherapy
Decompensation triggers: ischemia, infection, arrhythmia, missed diuretics, NSAIDs

rows.label: Clues
items: Orthopnea, paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, elevated JVP, crackles, dependent edema
S3 suggests volume overload; S4 suggests stiff ventricle
★ **Flash edema**: abrupt respiratory distress, severe hypertension, pink frothy sputum

rows.label: Pathophys
items: RAAS/sympathetic activation → vasoconstriction, sodium retention, adverse remodeling
Nonosmotic **ADH** release → dilutional hyponatremia; marker of advanced disease

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Echocardiography**: EF, valves, wall motion; ECG, CXR, BNP support diagnosis
Low BNP argues against HF; obesity lowers BNP, renal dysfunction raises it
Identify precipitant: troponin, CBC, electrolytes, creatinine; evaluate ischemic cause

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Acute congestion → **IV furosemide**; hypoxemia → oxygen; respiratory distress → noninvasive ventilation
★ Hypertensive pulmonary edema → **IV nitroglycerin**; shock → norepinephrine ± dobutamine, urgent cause correction
Start beta-blocker only when compensated; ACE inhibitor → ARNI requires 36-hour washout
MRA requires eGFR >30, K <5; persistent EF ≤35% despite GDMT → consider ICD

rows.label: Complications
items: Cardiorenal syndrome, ventricular arrhythmia, sudden death, hepatic congestion
Diuresis → hypokalemia; RAAS blockade → hyperkalemia, renal dysfunction; monitor creatinine/K

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Daily weights, sodium moderation, adherence; **continue GDMT after EF recovery**
Treat hypertension, CAD, AF; smoking cessation, exercise, influenza/pneumococcal vaccination

rows.label: Mimics
items: COPD: obstructive spirometry, hyperinflation
Nephrotic syndrome: heavy proteinuria, hypoalbuminemia
PE: pleuritic pain, thrombotic risk, RV strain

heart-failure.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [ACC HFrEF 2024](https://www.acc.org/Latest-in-Cardiology/ten-points-to-remember/2024/03/06/19/22/2024-acc-expert-consensus-hfref); other points established teaching.

humeral-fractures.name: Humeral fractures
humeral-fractures.scope: Proximal humerus fracture (axillary nerve), humeral shaft fracture (radial nerve, wrist drop), neurologic assessment, coaptation splint, functional brace, surgical fixation indications
humeral-fractures.core: Humeral fracture management depends on location, displacement, and neurovascular injury; document nerve function before and after manipulation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Older adults with osteoporosis: low-energy proximal fractures; younger adults: high-energy trauma
Shaft injuries from direct blow, twisting, falls; consider malignancy with minimal-trauma shaft fracture

rows.label: Clues
items: Upper-arm pain, swelling, ecchymosis, deformity; reduced shoulder/elbow motion
★ Proximal/surgical neck injury → **axillary nerve**: lateral shoulder numbness, impaired deltoid function
★ Shaft injury → **radial nerve**: wrist/finger extension weakness, dorsal first-web-space sensory loss
Cold pulseless hand, expanding hematoma, severe stretch pain → urgent vascular/compartment evaluation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Axillary nerve wraps around surgical neck; radial nerve travels along the spiral groove
Closed-fracture radial palsy often reflects neurapraxia and recovers without immediate exploration

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **AP/lateral humerus radiographs including shoulder and elbow**; dedicated joint views when involved
Check pulses, capillary refill, motor/sensory function of radial, median, ulnar, and axillary nerves
Repeat examination after reduction/splinting; CT for complex proximal/articular fracture planning
Open wound near fracture → evaluate as open fracture even if bone not visible

rows.label: Tx
items: Analgesia, immobilization, ice; open injury → IV cefazolin, tetanus protection, urgent irrigation/debridement
★ Most closed shaft fractures → **coaptation splint**, then functional brace after swelling subsides
Minimally displaced proximal fracture → sling, early supervised range of motion to limit stiffness
Displaced complex proximal patterns → fixation or selected arthroplasty depending on age and reconstructability
★ Surgery: **open fracture, vascular injury, floating elbow**, unacceptable alignment, failed bracing/nonunion

rows.label: Complications
items: Radial nerve palsy, malunion/nonunion; proximal injuries: avascular necrosis, shoulder stiffness
Secondary/new palsy after reduction or penetrating injury → urgent specialist reassessment, possible exploration

rows.label: Prevention
items: Fall reduction, osteoporosis evaluation after fragility fracture; rehabilitation preserves joint motion
No prolonged unmonitored sling use; regular alignment and neurovascular follow-up

rows.label: Mimics
items: Shoulder dislocation: altered contour and displaced humeral head on joint views
Rotator cuff tear: weakness without fracture, especially persistent after healing

humeral-fractures.evidence: Not checked online; established orthopedic teaching.

hypercalcemia.name: Hypercalcemia
hypercalcemia.scope: Primary hyperparathyroidism, malignancy-associated hypercalcemia, milk-alkali syndrome, IV saline resuscitation, calcitonin, bisphosphonates
hypercalcemia.core: Elevated calcium causes stones, constipation, polyuria, weakness, and neuropsychiatric changes; PTH distinguishes hormone-driven disease from other causes.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Parathyroid adenoma/hyperplasia, malignancy, prolonged immobilization
Thiazides, lithium, excess vitamin D or calcium/absorbable alkali, granulomatous disease

rows.label: Clues
items: Dehydration, nausea, abdominal pain, reduced reflexes; ECG may show shortened QT
★ **Calcium >14 mg/dL**, confusion, arrhythmia, or severe volume depletion → urgent treatment
Primary hyperparathyroidism often asymptomatic; malignancy-associated disease tends to progress rapidly

rows.label: Pathophys
items: PTH promotes bone resorption and renal calcium retention while increasing phosphate excretion
Hypercalcemia impairs renal concentration → dehydration, reduced calcium clearance, self-reinforcing elevation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Confirm with repeat total/albumin-adjusted or **ionized calcium**, especially with altered proteins or critical illness
★ **Intact PTH first**; elevated or inappropriately normal → PTH-dependent
Suppressed PTH → PTHrP, vitamin D metabolites, malignancy/myeloma evaluation guided by context
Primary disease versus FHH → urine calcium; clearance ratio <0.01 favors FHH, with overlap
Parathyroid imaging localizes before surgery; never establishes biochemical diagnosis

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Severe/symptomatic → **IV isotonic saline**, then calcitonin for rapid temporary lowering
★ **IV zoledronic acid** for sustained malignancy control; denosumab if severe renal limitations/refractory disease
Calcitriol-mediated disease → glucocorticoids; dialysis for refractory life-threatening elevation or inability to hydrate
Primary disease: surgery for symptoms, age <50, calcium >1 above ULN, osteoporosis/fracture, stones, eGFR <60
Stop causative supplements/drugs; loop diuretic only for fluid overload, not routine calcium elimination

rows.label: Complications
items: Nephrolithiasis, nephrocalcinosis, AKI, osteoporosis/fractures, pancreatitis
Calcitonin tachyphylaxis after 48–72 hours; antiresorptives can cause hypocalcemia

rows.label: Prevention
items: Hydration, avoid excess calcium/alkali; monitor calcium, renal function, and bone density when observing primary disease

rows.label: Mimics
items: FHH: lifelong mild elevation, family history, hypocalciuria; surgery ineffective
Pseudohypercalcemia: high protein-bound calcium but normal ionized fraction

hypercalcemia.evidence: Not checked online; established calcium evaluation and emergency management.

hyperglycemic-crises.name: Hyperglycemic crises
hyperglycemic-crises.core: Insulin-deficient diabetes with osmotic diuresis: rapid acidotic illness or slowly progressive hyperosmolar encephalopathy.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Infection, missed insulin, pump failure, MI; DKA often type 1, HHS often older type 2
Euglycemic triggers: **SGLT2 inhibitors**, pregnancy, fasting

rows.label: Clues
items: Polyuria, thirst, weight loss, dry mucosa, tachycardia
DKA: abdominal pain, vomiting, **Kussmaul breathing**; HHS: profound dehydration, focal deficits
★ Severe: **hypotension, stupor**, or coma → ICU

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Insulin deficit + counterregulatory hormones → lipolysis, ketogenesis; residual insulin in HHS limits ketosis
Total-body K depleted despite initially normal/high serum K

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Glucose, electrolytes, venous pH, β-hydroxybutyrate**, osmolality; ECG + trigger evaluation
Effective osmolality = 2 × Na + glucose/18; glucose in mg/dL
★ HHS: **effective osmolality >300 OR total >320 mOsm/kg**; substantial ketosis/acidosis → mixed DKA/HHS
DKA resolution: ketones <0.6 mmol/L AND (pH ≥7.3 OR HCO₃ ≥18); urine ketones/anion gap misleading

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **IV isotonic crystalloid → K correction → IV regular insulin**; K <3.5 mmol/L → delay insulin
Replace K when <5 mmol/L; glucose checks every 1–2 h, electrolytes/pH/ketones every 4 h
★ Add **dextrose** below glucose 250; euglycemic presentation → immediately; continue insulin until crisis resolves
SC basal insulin overlaps infusion 1–2 h; bicarbonate only consider pH <7.0; HHS: slower osmolar correction

rows.label: Complications
items: AKI, thrombosis; treatment: hypoglycemia, hypokalemic arrhythmias, cerebral edema, hyperchloremic acidosis

rows.label: Prevention
items: Sick-day fluids/ketone checks; continue basal insulin; ensure supplies and early follow-up
Hold SGLT2 inhibitors during acute illness and before surgery

rows.label: Mimics
items: Alcoholic ketoacidosis: binge then poor intake; usually no diabetes
Starvation ketosis: usually milder acidosis, no marked hyperglycemia
Toxic alcohols: osmolar gap, exposure; absent substantial ketonemia

macrocytic-anemia.name: Macrocytic anemia
macrocytic-anemia.scope: Folate deficiency, vitamin B12 deficiency, pernicious anemia, hypersegmented neutrophils, methylmalonic acid and homocysteine
macrocytic-anemia.core: MCV >100 fL prompts separation of megaloblastic DNA-synthesis failure from alcohol, liver disease, hypothyroidism, reticulocytosis, and marrow disorders.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Vegan diet without supplementation, gastric bypass, ileal disease/resection, metformin → B12 depletion
Alcohol misuse, poor intake, pregnancy, methotrexate, trimethoprim → folate depletion
Autoimmune gastritis → pernicious anemia; nitrous oxide functionally inactivates cobalamin

rows.label: Clues
items: Fatigue, pallor, glossitis; ineffective erythropoiesis may raise LDH/indirect bilirubin and lower other cell lines
★ **Paresthesias, gait ataxia, impaired vibration/proprioception** → B12 deficiency, even without anemia
Smooth macro-ovalocytes and hypersegmented neutrophils indicate megaloblastic change

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Defective thymidine synthesis delays nuclear maturation relative to cytoplasm
B12-dependent myelin metabolism explains spinal cord/peripheral nerve injury; folate deficiency lacks this syndrome

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **CBC, smear, reticulocytes, B12**; assess folate, liver tests, TSH, exposures
Borderline B12 → methylmalonic acid; renal impairment can elevate it independently
★ Suspected pernicious anemia → **anti-intrinsic-factor antibodies**; highly specific but not fully sensitive
High reticulocytes → bleeding/hemolysis; unexplained cytopenias/dysplasia → bone marrow evaluation for MDS
Coexisting iron deficiency may normalize MCV; neurologic suspicion still requires B12 evaluation

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Replace B12 before or with folate**; folate alone can conceal ongoing neurologic injury
Neurologic/severe deficiency or malabsorption → parenteral B12 initially; irreversible cause requires lifelong replacement
Dietary B12 deficiency may respond to high-dose oral replacement; folate deficiency → oral folic acid
Remove causative drug/exposure where possible; monitor reticulocyte response and count recovery

rows.label: Complications
items: Untreated B12 deficiency → irreversible neurologic disability; severe disease → pancytopenia
Pernicious anemia → increased gastric adenocarcinoma and neuroendocrine tumor risk

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Reliable B12 supplementation for vegans**; lifelong monitoring/replacement after relevant GI surgery
Folic acid before conception and early pregnancy; improve nutrition and reduce harmful alcohol intake

rows.label: Mimics
items: Alcohol-associated macrocytosis: round macrocytes, no required megaloblastic change
Myelodysplasia: persistent multilineage cytopenia, dysplastic marrow
Reticulocytosis: polychromasia after blood loss or hemolysis

macrocytic-anemia.evidence: Not checked online; established hematology and nutritional teaching.

occupational-lung-disease.name: Occupational lung disease
occupational-lung-disease.scope: Silicosis, asbestosis, coal workers' pneumoconiosis, berylliosis
occupational-lung-disease.core: Progressive exertional dyspnea and interstitial lung abnormalities years after dust exposure require a detailed occupational history and exposure-specific imaging interpretation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Cumulative inhaled mineral dust, inadequate respiratory protection, mining/construction/manufacturing exposures
Long latency permits disease after retirement; smoking adds obstructive disease and cancer risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Dry cough, exertional breathlessness, reduced exercise capacity; examination may show crackles
Advanced disease: resting hypoxemia, cyanosis, clubbing or right-heart strain
Pleural plaques mark exposure but often do not explain substantial functional impairment

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Persistent particles activate macrophages and profibrotic pathways → irreversible interstitial scarring
Beryllium triggers a delayed cellular immune response with noncaseating granulomas

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Detailed job/task history + chest imaging**; HRCT clarifies radiograph findings
PFTs often restrictive with reduced DLCO; obstructive or mixed patterns can occur
★ Beryllium suspicion → **beryllium lymphocyte proliferation test**; biopsy may show granulomas
★ Silica exposure → **TB assessment**; evaluate fever, weight loss, cavitation for active infection
New unilateral pleural effusion, nodular pleural thickening, or mass → malignancy workup, tissue diagnosis

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Stop further exposure**, smoking cessation; oxygen for hypoxemia, pulmonary rehabilitation
Vaccination and prompt infection treatment; bronchodilators if coexisting airflow obstruction
Symptomatic progressive berylliosis → systemic glucocorticoids; no proven reversal of established dust fibrosis
Advanced refractory respiratory failure → lung transplant evaluation; treat TB or cancer separately

rows.label: Complications
items: Progressive massive fibrosis, pulmonary hypertension, cor pulmonale, respiratory failure
Asbestos: bronchogenic carcinoma and mesothelioma; smoking synergizes lung carcinoma risk, not mesothelioma
Silicosis: TB/nontuberculous mycobacterial infection, lung cancer

rows.label: Prevention
items: Engineering dust controls, wet cutting, fitted respirators, occupational surveillance
Protect household contacts from contaminated work clothing; adherence to workplace exposure limits

rows.label: Mimics
items: Sarcoidosis: granulomas without relevant exposure; beryllium test negative
Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis: basal subpleural honeycombing without causative occupational history
Heart failure: congestion/effusions with cardiac dysfunction

occupational-lung-disease.evidence: Not checked online; established occupational pulmonary medicine teaching.

pericardial-disease.name: Pericardial disease
pericardial-disease.scope: Acute pericarditis, pericardial effusion, tamponade, constrictive pericarditis
pericardial-disease.core: Pericardial inflammation, fluid accumulation, or fibrosis produces distinct chest-pain and impaired-filling syndromes; hemodynamic effect depends on accumulation rate.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Viral/idiopathic, autoimmune disease, uremia, malignancy, TB, radiation, cardiac surgery
Early post-MI inflammation or delayed immune-mediated Dressler syndrome; trauma/anticoagulation can cause hemopericardium

rows.label: Clues
items: Pericarditis: sharp pleuritic positional pain, better leaning forward; friction rub may be transient
★ Tamponade: **hypotension, elevated JVP, muffled sounds**, pulsus paradoxus >10 mmHg; triad often incomplete
Constrictive disease: edema/ascites, Kussmaul sign, pericardial knock, prominent y descent

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Inflamed surfaces cause pain; fluid or scar limits diastolic filling and stroke volume
Tamponade equalizes diastolic pressures; constriction exaggerates ventricular interdependence with respiration

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Pericarditis: ≥2 of **typical pain, rub, diffuse ST elevation/PR depression, new effusion**
Troponin elevation suggests myocardial involvement; CRP supports inflammation; echo assesses fluid and ventricular function
★ **Urgent bedside echo** for suspected tamponade: right-sided chamber collapse, plethoric IVC
Constrictive suspicion → echo, CT/MRI for thickening/calcification; catheterization if diagnosis remains uncertain

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Tamponade → **urgent pericardiocentesis**; IV fluids bridge; avoid diuresis/positive-pressure ventilation
Purulent/traumatic effusion or recurrent difficult drainage → surgical drainage/window; antibiotics for bacterial cause
Stable effusion → treat cause, serial echo; low voltage alone never determines drainage
High-risk features → admit: fever, large effusion, immunosuppression, anticoagulation, subacute onset, NSAID failure

rows.label: Complications
items: Recurrent inflammation, arrhythmia/myocarditis, obstructive shock; procedural drainage → cardiac injury
Rapid decompression can rarely cause ventricular dysfunction; NSAIDs → GI/renal injury, colchicine → diarrhea

rows.label: Prevention
items: Colchicine course: first episode 3 months; recurrence ≥6 months; taper anti-inflammatory drugs after remission
Exercise restriction until clinical/inflammatory resolution; optimize dialysis for uremic disease

rows.label: Mimics
items: STEMI: regional ST elevation with reciprocal changes; urgent coronary evaluation if uncertain
Restrictive cardiomyopathy: myocardial disease, less respiratory ventricular discordance
PE: thrombotic risk, acute RV strain

table.title: Nonemergency definitive management
rows: Ibuprofen + colchicine; aspirin preferred after MI
Selected low-dose glucocorticoid or IL-1 blockade

pleural-effusion.name: Pleural effusion
pleural-effusion.scope: Transudate vs exudate (Light criteria), parapneumonic effusion, empyema, malignant effusion
pleural-effusion.core: Fluid in the pleural space causes dyspnea, dullness, and reduced breath sounds; classify by mechanism and identify infection requiring drainage.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Heart failure, cirrhosis, nephrotic syndrome; pneumonia, malignancy, pulmonary embolism, TB
Recent thoracic surgery, pancreatitis, esophageal rupture, autoimmune disease

rows.label: Clues
items: Pleuritic pain, reduced tactile fremitus; large effusion may shift mediastinum away
Fever or persistent sepsis despite antibiotics suggests complicated parapneumonic fluid
Bloody fluid suggests malignancy, embolism, or trauma; milky fluid suggests chyle

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Transudate: altered hydrostatic/oncotic pressure; exudate: increased permeability or impaired lymphatic drainage

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Chest radiograph → **ultrasound-guided thoracentesis** for new unexplained, unilateral, or atypical effusion
Classic bilateral heart-failure effusions → diuresis first; sample if fever, asymmetry, or treatment failure
★ **Exudate if any Light criterion** positive; compare paired pleural and serum measurements
Pleural pH, glucose, cell differential, Gram stain/culture; cytology if cancer suspected
Diuresis can create pseudoexudate; serum–pleural albumin gradient >1.2 g/dL supports transudate

rows.label: Tx
items: Treat systemic cause; therapeutic thoracentesis for significant symptoms; avoid rapid excessive drainage
★ Pus, positive culture, or **pH ≤7.20** → chest tube plus antibiotics
Loculated infected fluid → intrapleural tPA/DNase; persistent sepsis → VATS evaluation
★ Recurrent symptomatic malignancy → **indwelling pleural catheter** or pleurodesis; trapped lung favors catheter

rows.label: Complications
items: Empyema, loculation, trapped lung, respiratory compromise
Thoracentesis → pneumothorax, bleeding, reexpansion pulmonary edema

rows.label: Prevention
items: Heart-failure control, prompt pneumonia treatment; ultrasound guidance reduces procedural injury

rows.label: Mimics
items: Atelectasis: mediastinal shift toward volume loss
Consolidation: increased fremitus, bronchial breath sounds
Pneumothorax: hyperresonance rather than dullness

pleural-effusion.evidence: Not checked online; established pleural disease teaching.

pneumonia.name: Pneumonia
pneumonia.scope: Community-acquired, hospital-acquired, ventilator-associated, aspiration, atypical pneumonia (Legionella, Mycoplasma)
pneumonia.core: Acute lower respiratory infection with a new infiltrate; severity, acquisition setting, and resistance risks determine disposition and empiric antibiotics.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Smoking, COPD, age, immunosuppression; dysphagia or impaired consciousness → aspiration
HAP ≥48 hours hospitalized; VAP ≥48 hours after intubation
Prior MRSA/Pseudomonas isolation or recent hospitalization with IV antibiotics → resistant pathogens

rows.label: Clues
items: Fever, cough, sputum, focal crackles; older adults may present with confusion
★ Severe: **hypoxemia, hypotension, tachypnea**, multilobar disease; ventilation or pressors → ICU
Legionella: water exposure, diarrhea, hyponatremia; Mycoplasma: young adults, dry cough, cold agglutinins

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Alveolar inflammation/exudate → shunt and impaired oxygenation
Chemical aspiration pneumonitis: sterile gastric injury; rapid improvement possible without antibiotics

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **CXR** first; CT if strong suspicion despite nondiagnostic radiograph
PSI supports admission decisions; severe CAP → blood/sputum cultures, Legionella urine antigen ± respiratory PCR
Low procalcitonin alone does not justify withholding initial antibiotics in radiographically confirmed bacterial CAP

rows.label: Tx
items: Oxygen, fluids for hypoperfusion; drain empyema; narrow antibiotics to cultures
★ Aspiration pneumonia: usual CAP coverage; **add anaerobic coverage only for abscess/empyema**
Stable nonsevere CAP: ATS 2025 permits 3–4 days; classic ≥5-day rule remains for severe disease
★ Severe noninfluenza CAP → consider **systemic corticosteroids**; nonsevere CAP → avoid routine steroids

rows.label: Complications
items: Parapneumonic effusion, empyema, abscess, bacteremia, respiratory failure, sepsis
Postinfluenza S aureus → necrotizing pneumonia; antibiotic exposure → C difficile

rows.label: Prevention
items: Influenza/pneumococcal vaccination, smoking cessation, swallowing evaluation
VAP prevention: head elevation, oral care, early liberation from ventilation

rows.label: Mimics
items: PE: thrombotic risk, pleuritic pain, no infectious source
HF: bilateral edema, elevated JVP, cardiac dysfunction

table.title: Empiric adult regimens
rows: Amoxicillin/clavulanate + azithromycin; doxycycline alternative; or levofloxacin

skin-cancer.name: Skin cancer
skin-cancer.scope: Actinic keratosis, squamous cell carcinoma, basal cell carcinoma, melanoma, photoprotection and sunscreen
skin-cancer.core: Changing pigmented lesions or persistent keratinizing, pearly, or ulcerated growths require examination and tissue diagnosis rather than empiric reassurance.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: UV exposure, fair skin, sunburns, tanning beds, older age; immunosuppression particularly increases SCC
Melanoma: numerous/atypical nevi, family/personal melanoma history; may arise without a preexisting nevus
Chronic wounds/scars predispose SCC; acral melanoma occurs regardless of skin pigmentation

rows.label: Clues
items: ★ Melanoma: **ABCDE**—asymmetry, border irregularity, color variation, diameter, evolution; ugly-duckling lesion
Diameter >6 mm concerning, but smaller evolving lesions still require biopsy
Amelanotic melanoma may be pink; inspect soles, palms, nail beds; nail pigment extending onto fold concerning
Rapid growth, bleeding, nonhealing ulcer, fixation, neurologic symptoms, nodes → aggressive or advanced disease

rows.label: Pathophys
items: UV-induced DNA damage → keratinocyte malignancy; melanocyte transformation causes melanoma
AK represents dysplastic keratinocytes with potential progression to invasive SCC

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Suspicious melanoma → **full-thickness excisional biopsy with narrow margins** to measure Breslow depth
Partial biopsy acceptable when complete excision impractical; avoid superficial sampling that prevents staging
Suspected keratinocyte carcinoma → shave, punch, or excisional biopsy deep enough to assess invasion
Breslow thickness/ulceration guide melanoma staging; sentinel-node discussion generally at ≥0.8 mm or ulceration

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Localized invasive cancers → **surgical excision**; high-risk/recurrent facial BCC/SCC → Mohs
★ Melanoma → **wide local excision after diagnostic biopsy**; margins depend on depth
Advanced melanoma → specialist immunotherapy, selected BRAF-targeted drugs; avoid destructive treatment before diagnosis

rows.label: Complications
items: BCC: extensive local destruction, rare metastasis; SCC: nodal metastasis, especially high-risk sites/immunosuppression
Melanoma: distant metastases, including brain; immunotherapy → colitis, endocrinopathies, pneumonitis

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Broad-spectrum SPF ≥30**, reapply every 2 hours/outdoors after swimming; shade, protective clothing, no tanning
Self-examination, postcancer follow-up; suspicious lesions require evaluation despite uncertain population-screening benefit

rows.label: Mimics
items: Seborrheic keratosis: waxy stuck-on plaque; atypical lesions still biopsy
Dermatofibroma: firm papule with dimple sign
Benign nevus: stable symmetric uniform appearance

table.title: Nonmelanoma patterns
rows: Assess high-risk features and regional nodes
Pearly rolled edge, telangiectasia, central ulcer
Treat despite slow growth; local invasion

skin-cancer.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [AAD melanoma guidance](https://www.aad.org/member/clinical-quality/guidelines/melanoma); established keratinocyte-cancer and photoprotection teaching.

stable-ischemic-heart-disease.name: Stable ischemic heart disease
stable-ischemic-heart-disease.scope: Stable angina pectoris, exercise stress testing, stress echocardiography, antianginal pharmacotherapy, invasive coronary angiography indications
stable-ischemic-heart-disease.core: Predictable exertional chest pressure relieved by rest reflects myocardial oxygen supply–demand mismatch; new rest symptoms require acute coronary syndrome evaluation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Smoking, diabetes, hypertension, dyslipidemia, CKD, older age, family history of premature CAD
Anemia, tachycardia, and uncontrolled blood pressure can worsen ischemic symptoms

rows.label: Clues
items: Substernal squeezing, arm/jaw radiation; dyspnea may be an anginal equivalent
Normal resting ECG does not exclude CAD; examination often normal between episodes
★ **Crescendo symptoms, prolonged pain, rest pain**, instability → ECG/troponins and ACS pathway

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Flow-limiting coronary atherosclerosis restricts supply when demand rises
Microvascular dysfunction can produce ischemia despite absence of obstructive epicardial disease

rows.label: Dx
items: Resting ECG, lipid profile, HbA1c, renal function; estimate clinical likelihood before choosing testing
★ Selected intermediate-risk suspected CAD → **CCTA or stress testing**, based on suitability
★ **Coronary angiography** for high-risk noninvasive findings, refractory limiting symptoms, or suspected high-risk anatomy
No routine repeated anatomic/stress testing in stable asymptomatic patients without functional change

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Relief → **sublingual nitroglycerin**; avoid with recent PDE-5 inhibitor use or hypotension
★ Prevention → **aspirin + high-intensity statin**; manage BP/diabetes, lifestyle and exercise
Antianginal first-line: beta blocker or calcium-channel blocker; persistent symptoms → long-acting nitrate or ranolazine
Beta blockers improve outcomes for selected recent MI/reduced EF indications, not all stable CAD indefinitely
Refractory symptoms → revascularization; CABG improves survival in left-main/selected complex multivessel disease

rows.label: Complications
items: MI, heart failure, malignant arrhythmia, sudden death
Nitrates → headache/hypotension; combining beta blocker with verapamil/diltiazem can cause bradycardia/heart block

rows.label: Prevention
items: Smoking cessation, Mediterranean-style diet, habitual activity; cardiac rehabilitation when eligible
ACE inhibitor/ARB when hypertension, diabetes, CKD, or reduced EF; adherence and lipid follow-up

rows.label: Mimics
items: GERD: meal/recumbency association, regurgitation
Aortic stenosis: exertional symptoms with systolic murmur
Costochondritis: reproducible focal chest-wall tenderness

table.title: Functional test selection
rows: Exercise stress echocardiography or perfusion imaging

stable-ischemic-heart-disease.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [ACC chronic coronary disease guideline summary (2023)](https://www.acc.org/latest-in-cardiology/ten-points-to-remember/2023/07/17/19/06/2023-guideline-for-chronic-coronary-disease-gl-ccd/).

study-designs.name: Study designs
study-designs.scope: Case-control, cohort, cross-sectional, RCT, control selection, bias, internal and external validity
study-designs.core: Study design determines how participants are selected, when exposure/outcome are measured, and which associations can be estimated without avoidable bias.

rows.label: Definition
items: Internal validity: credible within-study inference; external validity: applicability elsewhere

rows.label: Interpret
items: ★ **Randomization balances confounders on average**; concealed allocation prevents enrollment bias
Blinding reduces behavior/assessment bias; intention-to-treat retains original randomized groups
Loss to follow-up can bias estimates when related to exposure and outcome

rows.label: Use when
items: ★ Case-control controls → **same source population** that produced cases, independent of exposure
Prospective measurement improves temporality but does not eliminate confounding in observational research

rows.label: Compare
items: Confounding: third-variable distortion; randomize, restrict, match, stratify, or adjust
Effect modification: association differs across strata; report rather than remove it

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Case-control sampling cannot directly estimate incidence or risk** without additional population data
★ Cross-sectional data lack reliable **temporal sequence**; prevalent cases favor longer survivors
Random selection supports generalizability; random assignment supports causal inference

study-designs.evidence: Established epidemiologic definitions; no clinical guideline involved.

type-2-diabetes-mellitus.name: Type 2 diabetes mellitus
type-2-diabetes-mellitus.scope: Diagnosis, glycemic targets, pharmacotherapy (metformin contraindications, SGLT2i, GLP-1 RA, insulin), chronic complications screening, pediatric screening in obesity
type-2-diabetes-mellitus.core: Insulin resistance with progressive beta-cell failure produces chronic hyperglycemia and vascular injury, often preceding obvious symptoms.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Central obesity, family history, prior gestational diabetes, PCOS, physical inactivity
Glucocorticoids and atypical antipsychotics can unmask dysglycemia

rows.label: Clues
items: Polyuria, polydipsia, blurred vision, recurrent candidiasis; acanthosis nigricans suggests marked insulin resistance
Weight loss, ketosis, or dehydration → severe insulin deficiency; reconsider diabetes type

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Impaired peripheral glucose uptake + excess hepatic glucose output; relative insulin secretion becomes inadequate

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **A1c ≥6.5%**, fasting glucose ≥126, or 2-hour OGTT ≥200 mg/dL
Random glucose ≥200 with classic symptoms also diagnostic; otherwise confirm with second abnormal result
A1c unreliable with altered erythrocyte survival; use plasma glucose
★ Youth: screen puberty/age 10, whichever earlier, with overweight/obesity + additional risk; repeat ≥every 2 years

rows.label: Tx
items: Lifestyle + metformin when suitable; GI intolerance, B12 deficiency; avoid eGFR <30, AKI, hypoxia
Do not newly start metformin below eGFR 45; reassess/reduce existing use at 30–44
★ HF/CKD → **SGLT2 inhibitor**; ASCVD/obesity → GLP-1 RA, independent of A1c or metformin
★ Catabolism, glucose ≥300, or A1c >10% → **insulin**; otherwise GLP-1 RA preferred before insulin
Adults: A1c <7%, fasting 80–130, postmeal <180; relax for frailty/hypoglycemia; quarterly checks until stable

rows.label: Complications
items: Retinopathy, nephropathy, neuropathy, foot ulceration; coronary, cerebral, and peripheral arterial disease
SGLT2 inhibitors: genital mycoses, euglycemic DKA; sulfonylureas/insulin: hypoglycemia, weight gain

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ At diagnosis then annually: **urine albumin/creatinine, eGFR, foot examination**; arrange retinal examination
Retinal follow-up by findings; statin by cardiovascular risk; ACE inhibitor/ARB for hypertension with albuminuria

rows.label: Mimics
items: Type 1 diabetes: autoantibodies, low C-peptide, abrupt ketosis
Diabetes insipidus: dilute polyuria without elevated blood glucose

urinary-tract-infections.name: Urinary tract infections
urinary-tract-infections.scope: Asymptomatic bacteriuria, acute cystitis, pyelonephritis, catheter-associated urinary tract infection (CAUTI), catheter removal, empiric antibiotics
urinary-tract-infections.core: Symptoms localize urinary infection: bladder disease lacks systemic illness; renal involvement causes fever or flank pain; bacteriuria alone is insufficient.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Sexual activity, spermicides, pregnancy, obstruction/stones, urinary retention, instrumentation
Catheter duration, diabetes, prior resistant isolates or antibiotics increase complicated-course risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Dysuria, frequency, urgency, suprapubic discomfort; absent vaginal discharge supports urinary source
★ **Rigors, CVA tenderness, vomiting, hypotension** → pyelonephritis or urosepsis
Catheterized patients: new urinary/systemic symptoms; cloudy urine or pyuria alone insufficient

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Usually ascending enteric bacteria, predominantly E coli; catheter biofilm maintains colonization
Urease-producing Proteus alkalinizes urine → struvite calculi and persistent infection

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Urinalysis**: pyuria, leukocyte esterase, nitrites; negative nitrites do not exclude infection
Culture: pyelonephritis, pregnancy, CAUTI, recurrence/resistance; classic cystitis often clinical
Persistent fever after 48–72 hours, sepsis, or suspected obstruction → renal imaging
Asymptomatic bacteriuria: usually ≥100,000 CFU/mL; delirium alone → seek other causes without automatic antibiotics

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Treat asymptomatic bacteriuria only in pregnancy or before urologic mucosal trauma** in routine adult scenarios
★ CAUTI → **remove unnecessary catheter**; if needed and present >2 weeks, replace before culture/treatment
★ Infected obstructed collecting system → **urgent drainage + IV antibiotics**; antibiotics alone insufficient
Improving nonpregnant pyelonephritis: fluoroquinolone 5–7 days, other active drugs 7 days; high-risk cases individualized

rows.label: Complications
items: Bacteremia, septic shock, renal/perinephric abscess; pregnancy → preterm birth
Antibiotics → resistance, C difficile; fluoroquinolones → tendon injury, QT prolongation

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid unnecessary catheters; closed drainage, daily removal assessment
Postmenopausal recurrence → vaginal estrogen; selected recurrences → postcoital/continuous antibiotic prophylaxis

rows.label: Mimics
items: Vaginitis: discharge, pruritus, external burning
Urethritis: sexual exposure, discharge, positive gonorrhea/chlamydia NAAT
Bladder pain syndrome: chronic symptoms, repeatedly negative cultures

table.title: Initial antibiotics; tailor to culture/resistance
rows: Ciprofloxacin/levofloxacin; initial ceftriaxone if resistance risk
IV ceftriaxone; cefepime/piperacillin-tazobactam if Pseudomonas risk
Avoid nitrofurantoin/fosfomycin: inadequate renal tissue levels

valvular-heart-disease.name: Valvular heart disease
valvular-heart-disease.scope: Aortic stenosis, aortic regurgitation, mitral stenosis, mitral regurgitation, mitral valve prolapse, physical exam, echocardiography, surgical and transcatheter replacement
valvular-heart-disease.core: Murmur timing, location, radiation, and loading maneuvers localize valve disease; symptoms and ventricular response determine intervention.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Aging calcification/bicuspid valve → AS; rheumatic disease → MS
Endocarditis, aortic root dilation/dissection → AR; ischemia, prolapse, chamber dilation → MR

rows.label: Clues
items: Exertional dyspnea, pulmonary edema, reduced exercise tolerance; abrupt deterioration suggests acute regurgitation
★ **Exertional syncope, angina, or HF** with obstruction → severe symptomatic disease
Squatting/handgrip increase regurgitant murmurs; standing/Valsalva makes MVP click earlier

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Stenosis produces upstream pressure overload; regurgitation produces chamber volume overload
Acute regurgitation lacks compensatory dilation, rapidly elevating filling pressures and reducing forward output

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **TTE Doppler** defines anatomy, severity, EF, chamber dimensions, pulmonary pressures
Severe AS: velocity ≥4 m/s, mean gradient ≥40, or valve area ≤1 cm²; discordance requires reassessment
Severe MS: valve area ≤1.5 cm²; TEE for thrombus before balloon intervention or uncertain anatomy
★ Acute murmur with shock → **urgent echocardiography**; TEE if endocarditis/dissection suspected

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Acute severe AR/MR → **urgent surgery**, stabilize with afterload reduction/diuresis if BP permits
Severe primary MR: **EF ≤60% or LVESD ≥40 mm** triggers intervention even without symptoms
Secondary MR → optimize HF treatment first; selected persistent severe cases benefit from transcatheter edge-to-edge repair
Avoid excessive preload reduction in severe AS; symptomatic relief never replaces needed valve intervention

rows.label: Complications
items: Heart failure, pulmonary hypertension, AF, systemic embolism, endocarditis
Mechanical prosthesis: thrombosis/bleeding; bioprosthesis: structural degeneration

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **Warfarin for mechanical valves**; no DOAC substitution; rheumatic MS with AF also requires warfarin
Prosthetic valve or prior endocarditis → selected dental prophylaxis; native isolated MVP does not qualify
Periodic echo and symptom review; treat rheumatic fever to prevent recurrent valve injury

rows.label: Mimics
items: HCM: systolic murmur increases with Valsalva/standing
Aortic sclerosis: ejection murmur without significant gradient; flow murmur: normal valve anatomy

table.title: Valve signatures and definitive options
rows: Early diastolic decrescendo; wide pulse pressure
Suitable symptomatic rheumatic valve → balloon commissurotomy

valvular-heart-disease.evidence: Not checked online; established echo thresholds and intervention framework.

venous-thromboembolism.name: Venous thromboembolism
venous-thromboembolism.core: Unilateral swollen leg or sudden unexplained dyspnea with pleuritic pain; pulmonary embolism severity determined by hemodynamics, not clot size.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Immobilization, surgery, malignancy, estrogen, pregnancy/postpartum, previous VTE, inherited thrombophilia

rows.label: Clues
items: DVT: asymmetric calf tenderness, warmth; PE: tachycardia, hypoxemia, hemoptysis, sometimes normal oxygen saturation
Syncope, elevated JVP, cool extremities → impending RV failure; normal chest radiograph does not exclude PE

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Stasis/endothelial injury/hypercoagulability → venous clot; pulmonary obstruction → V/Q mismatch, RV pressure overload

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Wells/pretest probability** first; very low-risk + PERC-negative → no testing
★ Low/intermediate probability → **D-dimer**; negative excludes; positive/high probability → **CT pulmonary angiography**

rows.label: Complications
items: Postthrombotic syndrome; persistent dyspnea → evaluate chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension
Anticoagulation/thrombolysis → bleeding; heparin → HIT

rows.label: Prevention

Hospital prophylaxis: LMWH; active bleeding → intermittent pneumatic compression; early mobilization

rows.label: Mimics

ventricular-arrhythmias.name: Ventricular arrhythmias
ventricular-arrhythmias.scope: Ventricular tachycardia (monomorphic, polymorphic/torsades de pointes), ventricular fibrillation, QT prolongation, antiarrhythmics, defibrillation and cardioversion, magnesium sulfate
ventricular-arrhythmias.core: Wide-complex tachycardia is ventricular tachycardia until proven otherwise; pulse, stability, morphology, and QT determine immediate treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prior MI/scar, cardiomyopathy, acute ischemia, channelopathies, myocarditis
Low K/Mg, bradycardia, congenital long QT; macrolides, antipsychotics, methadone, class IA/III antiarrhythmics

rows.label: Clues
items: Palpitations, syncope, chest pain, dyspnea; pulseless collapse requires immediate arrest algorithm
★ **Shock, ischemia, altered mentation, acute HF** with sustained tachycardia → unstable
Torsades often follows pause-dependent long-short sequence; recurrent self-terminating runs can precede arrest

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Scar reentry often causes monomorphic VT; prolonged repolarization produces early afterdepolarizations and torsades
VF causes chaotic ineffective ventricular activation with no meaningful cardiac output

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Check pulse immediately**, attach monitor/defibrillator; 12-lead ECG only if stabilization not delayed
AV dissociation, capture/fusion beats, concordance favor VT over SVT with aberrancy
Measure baseline QTc, review drugs, electrolytes, ischemia; QTc >500 ms increases torsades risk

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Pulseless VT/VF → **unsynchronized defibrillation + CPR**, epinephrine; refractory shocks → amiodarone/lidocaine
★ Unstable monomorphic VT with pulse → **synchronized cardioversion**; sustained polymorphic VT → unsynchronized shock
Stable monomorphic VT → IV procainamide or amiodarone; avoid procainamide with prolonged QT/severe HF
★ Recurrent torsades → **IV magnesium**, stop QT drugs, replace K; acquired pause-dependent cases → overdrive pacing
Normal-QT polymorphic VT → treat ischemia, consider lidocaine/amiodarone; magnesium not routine

rows.label: Complications
items: Cardiac arrest, sudden death, hypoxic brain injury, cardiogenic shock
QT-prolonging antiarrhythmics can worsen torsades; cardioversion without synchronization can induce VF in organized rhythms

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ **ICD** for survivors without reversible cause; selected low-EF patients for primary prevention after optimization
Beta-blocker for chronic ischemic/structural risk; ablation for recurrent scar-related VT/ICD shocks
Correct reversible triggers; congenital long QT needs specialist beta-blocker/ICD risk assessment

rows.label: Mimics
items: SVT with aberrancy: prior bundle-branch pattern; uncertainty → treat as VT
Preexcited AF: irregular very rapid wide complexes; avoid AV nodal blockers
Artifact: palpable pulse and unaffected underlying QRS despite apparent chaotic tracing

viral-hepatitis.name: Viral hepatitis
viral-hepatitis.scope: Hepatitis A, B, C, D, E, serologic markers, acute vs chronic hepatitis, HCV antibody and RNA confirmatory testing, direct-acting antivirals, postexposure prophylaxis (HBIG and vaccine)
viral-hepatitis.core: Hepatocellular injury with malaise, anorexia, jaundice, and high aminotransferases prompts exposure-based viral testing; chronic infection may be clinically silent.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: HAV/HEV: fecal–oral spread; HBV/HCV/HDV: blood, perinatal exposure; HBV also sexual
Injection exposure, unscreened blood, endemic birth region; HDV requires HBV
HEV severe in pregnancy; perinatal HBV and most untreated HCV often become chronic

rows.label: Clues
items: Dark urine, pale stool, RUQ discomfort; transaminases often far exceed alkaline phosphatase
★ **Encephalopathy + INR ≥1.5 without preexisting cirrhosis** → acute liver failure
HBV: serum sickness, polyarteritis nodosa; HCV: mixed cryoglobulinemia, porphyria cutanea tarda

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Host immune injury to infected hepatocytes; persistent HBV/HCV → fibrosis and carcinogenesis
HBV nuclear templates persist; HCV cure does not confer immunity

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ HAV acute → **IgM anti-HAV**; total/IgG antibody indicates immunity
★ **HCV antibody → reflex HCV RNA**; antibody persists after clearance; recent exposure → RNA directly
HBsAg persisting >6 months → chronic HBV; HBV DNA quantifies replication
HEV testing by exposure/context; HBsAg-positive severe hepatitis → consider anti-HDV/HDV RNA
INR, bilirubin, creatinine; chronic disease → fibrosis staging, coinfection testing

rows.label: Tx
items: HAV, most HEV, uncomplicated acute HBV → supportive care; liver failure → urgent transplant center
★ Chronic HCV → **glecaprevir/pibrentasvir or sofosbuvir/velpatasvir**, usually 8–12 weeks; verify interactions/cirrhosis
Chronic HBV needing treatment → tenofovir or entecavir; severe acute HBV also may need antiviral
HCV cure: RNA undetectable ≥12 weeks after completion; do not delay treatment awaiting spontaneous resolution

rows.label: Complications
items: Fulminant hepatitis; chronic HBV/HCV → cirrhosis, portal hypertension, hepatocellular carcinoma
HBV can cause HCC without cirrhosis; DAAs may reactivate unrecognized HBV

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Susceptible HBV exposure → **HBIG + vaccine promptly**, preferably within 24 h; immunity determines exceptions
HAV exposure ≤2 weeks → vaccine; add immune globulin for immunocompromise/chronic liver disease
HAV/HBV vaccines, safer sex/injection practices; no HCV vaccine or proven HCV PEP
Cirrhosis/selected HBV → HCC surveillance with ultrasound ± AFP every 6 months

rows.label: Mimics
items: Drug-induced injury: medication/toxin relationship
Ischemic hepatitis: shock preceding abrupt marked aminotransferase rise
